text:
Connor McDavid has a 21-game point streak and the headlines are already reaching for the record book. That's the story in Edmonton, along with a coaching change that seems to have landed: Zach Hyman credited Mike Babcock with bringing new life to the room, and the Oilers are 15-3-3 with 33 points and about a coin flip to win the Pacific by our numbers.

Now the honest part. Edmonton has scored almost 20 more goals than its chances usually produce, and at five on five it has taken 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Our points model has them about nine points ahead of what their play has earned. The four-game winning streak came with 48% of the chances and 5.2 goals saved above expected in net.

Some of that is skill, and it's concentrated. Draisaitl, McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin have outscored teams 21-6 with 62% of the chances, and Evan Bouchard with Mattias Ekholm is 22-4. Behind them, the depth lines are losing their minutes badly.

Goaltending is the twist nobody planned for. Devon Levi, given up on in Buffalo, is 5-0-0 over his last five starts and posted his first career shutout in Toronto, while Tristan Jarry is at .942 over his own last five. What we'd watch: whether the depth catches up before the finishing cools, and whether Hyman's 500th career point comes soon.
